text: The 2022 loss of 0.6 ha (3.4%) in native forest (0.5 ha) was primarily due to small-scale clearing, as 0.2 ha of the loss occurred in patches under 0.5 ha—too small to be counted as a single event. The remaining 0.4 ha met the event threshold. The loss was confirmed by multiple sources: Hansen’s Global Forest Change (2025 update) detected the tree-cover loss, while the JRC’s 2020 reference data corroborated that the area was fully forested at baseline. Uruguay’s national forest cartography (MGAP 2021) confirmed the area was native forest, with no planted species present. No further details on the cause (e.g., logging, agriculture) are available from Earth observation alone.
